novel_features.name: Flow behavior coverage
novel_features.description: Shows how an Interview Flow actually routed across a whole study: every branch arm's share, how often the otherwise path fired, classifier errors, which steps interviews reached, and which declared variables are being captured. Flow-mode studies only: a linear study has no branch or flow records and correctly returns nothing.
novel_features.rationale: Branch decisions are returned by the per-interview transcript endpoint and never by bulk transcripts, so a study-level answer costs one request per interview — bounded, concurrent and reported here, instead of a researcher opening interviews one at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a branching interview might be misrouting: it names the arms that never fired and the share that fell through to the default, instead of making you read transcripts one at a time.
novel_features.group: Flow behavior you cannot see upstream

novel_features.name: Payout reconciliation
novel_features.description: Finds participants who completed a study but were never successfully notified, by joining completed interviews against the webhook deliveries that were supposed to tell your system about them.
novel_features.rationale: Spans two endpoint families with no server-side join, and the interesting set is an anti-join — the completions with no successful delivery — which only exists once both sides are local.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this after a payout or reward run to find the people your system was never told about, instead of trusting that every webhook landed.

novel_features.name: Study definition diff
novel_features.description: Compares two complete study definitions field by field — details, welcome and translations, screening, characteristics, questions or flow, recruitment — or compares a live study against a saved bundle file.
novel_features.rationale: Each side is roughly seven calls and nothing upstream diffs anything; the comparison only exists once both definitions are local.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before replaying a bundle over an existing study, or to see exactly how two studies' instruments differ.

novel_features.name: Answer rectangle
novel_features.description: Turns a study into a real table: one row per interview, one column per question or captured variable, with the external participant id as the join key and optional participant characteristic columns via --with-characteristics. Works for both linear and flow studies.
novel_features.rationale: No endpoint returns the interview by question rectangle; it is rebuilt locally from captured variables for flow studies and from the message stream for linear studies, since variables are empty for every linear study.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when you need to count or correlate answers rather than read them — it produces the rectangle you would otherwise rebuild by hand from transcripts.

novel_features.name: Flow effects audit
novel_features.description: Aggregates what a flow's side steps actually did across a study: failed data fetches with status codes, undelivered signals, and dry-run signals from simulations kept separate from real ones. Flow-mode studies only: a linear study has no branch or flow records and correctly returns nothing.
novel_features.rationale: Fetches and signals are exposed one interview at a time with no study-level endpoint, so triaging a broken integration means aggregating them locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an interview-time webhook or data fetch looks unreliable and you need the failures grouped by step rather than buried per interview.
novel_features.group: Flow behavior you cannot see upstream

novel_features.name: Study bundle export and apply
novel_features.description: Snapshots an entire study definition — details, welcome and translations, screening, characteristics, questions or flow, recruitment — into one file. The write half is a separate command, 'study apply --file <f>', which plans by default and writes only with --confirm, and which replays whole-resource sections only (question lists replay via 'studies questions').
novel_features.rationale: Authoring a study is roughly fifteen ordered API calls with nothing that captures the result; a single file makes the definition reviewable, versionable and replayable.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to clone or version a study definition instead of re-deriving fifteen calls; pair it with 'study diff' to see what a replay would change before running 'study apply --confirm'.

novel_features.name: Rehearsal vs reality diff
novel_features.description: Compares the simulated persona cohort against real participants on the same measures: step reach, branch arm mix, variable capture rate, message count and duration. Needs both cohorts; branch and variable measures are flow-mode only.
novel_features.rationale: Simulations deliberately mirror interviewer runtime semantics, but nothing server-side compares the two cohorts, so the comparison that turns a rehearsal into evidence has to be computed locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this after fielding starts to check whether real participants behave like the personas you rehearsed on, before trusting the pilot.
novel_features.group: Flow behavior you cannot see upstream

novel_features.name: Fielding burn rate
novel_features.description: Completions per day against the response quota, projecting the date the quota fills.
novel_features.rationale: Study stats and recruitment expose totals and quota but no rate anywhere in the API; the rate comes from the local time series of interview start times.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer whether a study will fill by a date, which the totals-only stats endpoint cannot tell you.

novel_features.name: Cross-tab
novel_features.description: Segments any scale or options question by any participant characteristic, with per-cell counts and per-segment completion rate.
novel_features.rationale: The platform collects characteristics specifically for segmentation, yet the scale and options tallies come back as flat value-to-count maps with no grouping parameter.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer whether an answer differs by segment — column marginals reconcile against the server's own tallies, so the numbers are checkable.

novel_features.name: Saturation curve
novel_features.description: Counts how many genuinely new terms each successive interview contributes, and marks the point where the curve flattens. A mechanical word-level proxy for new content, not a judgement about meaning.
novel_features.rationale: Requires chronological ordering of the full local transcript corpus; no endpoint has any concept of saturation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when deciding whether to stop fielding — it shows when additional interviews stopped adding new language, as evidence for that call rather than the call itself.

narrative.headline: Every Deutero endpoint, plus the flow-behaviour and fielding answers that take many API calls to assemble and that no single endpoint returns.
narrative.value_prop: Deutero's own MCP server already exposes every endpoint, so mirroring the API is table stakes. This CLI earns its place on the questions the API cannot answer in one call: how a branching Interview Flow actually routed across a study (`flow coverage`), the interview-by-question rectangle nobody returns (`answers matrix`), what a flow's fetches and signals really did (`flow effects`), which completions your webhook never reported (`reconcile`), and whether a study will fill by Thursday (`fielding`). Branch decisions come back one interview at a time and never in bulk, so these commands fan out for you — bounded, concurrent, and with the cost shown. They read live; `--limit` caps the fan-out at 500 interviews by default (raise it to at most 10,000). `sync` is separate and covers org-level resources only (projects, webhooks, webhook deliveries, embed keys, graph node types and health) — interviews and transcripts are study-scoped and cannot be synced.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set DEUTERO_API_KEY, or run 'deutero-pp-cli auth set-token'. The CLI sends it as an Authorization: Bearer header; the API accepts either an API key or a Stytch M2M access token there. (The API also accepts an X-API-Key header, but this CLI does not use it.) There is no browser or cookie login and no hosted setup URL — mint a key from the Deutero dashboard. 'auth status' shows what is configured.

quickstart.comment: Confirms DEUTERO_API_KEY is set and the host answers before anything else runs
Find the project you want; every study hangs off one
Get the study id the rest of the commands take
Totals and quota fill — the starting point the API does answer
The question no single API call answers: how the flow actually routed
The rectangle for counting and correlating, straight to a spreadsheet

troubleshoots.fix: Set DEUTERO_API_KEY. The CLI sends it as an Authorization: Bearer header; a Stytch M2M access token works there too.

troubleshoots.symptom: 403 'Access denied' on a study id you were given
troubleshoots.fix: The key belongs to one organization; a study in another org reads as denied. Run 'projects list' to see what this key can actually reach.

troubleshoots.symptom: First command after an idle period takes several seconds
troubleshoots.fix: The host cold-starts (~4s observed). Raise --timeout if you are scripting tight loops; subsequent calls return in well under a second.

troubleshoots.symptom: A study-wide command is slow on a large study
troubleshoots.fix: Branch decisions and flow effects exist only per interview, so these commands issue one request each. Lower --limit to bound the fan-out.

troubleshoots.symptom: flow coverage reports a branch arm as 'not observed'
troubleshoots.fix: That means no interview recorded taking it — not that it cannot fire. Captured answers and decisions are best-effort projections upstream.

troubleshoots.symptom: flow coverage or answers matrix returns nothing for a study
troubleshoots.fix: Linear studies have no flow records at all, and captured variables are empty for every linear study. answers matrix falls back to the message stream; flow coverage will correctly report nothing.

Those endpoints are scoped to a study id that sync cannot supply, so it syncs org-level resources only (projects, webhooks, webhook deliveries, embed keys, graph node types and health). The analysis commands read live and do not need sync.

troubleshoots.symptom: A step id in the output does not match anything in your flow editor
troubleshoots.fix: Report it — the API resolves compiled node ids back to your authored step ids, so a raw id like n3 is flagged in output rather than shown as a step name.

troubleshoots.symptom: flow coverage or rehearse diff returns empty branches for a study that clearly has questions
troubleshoots.fix: Those measures exist only in flow (graph) mode. A linear question-list study has no branch or variable records at all — answers matrix is the command for its answers.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when the question spans more than one Deutero API call: how a branching Interview Flow behaved across a study, the interview-by-question table no endpoint returns, whether a simulated rehearsal matched real participants, which completions a webhook never reported, and when a study will hit its quota. Also when you want a study definition as a file you can review, diff and replay. For single-resource reads and writes, an agent already holding Deutero's MCP server should use that instead.
anti_triggers: Conducting or moderating an interview — the AI interviewer does that, not this CLI
Recruiting participants or buying a panel
Analysing transcripts from a source other than Deutero
One-off single-endpoint reads when the Deutero MCP server is already connected

recipes.title: Find the branch that is misrouting
recipes.explanation: Narrows a large coverage report to just the signal that matters — which branch fell through to its default most often, and whether the classifier was erroring — instead of pulling the whole nested payload into context.

recipes.title: Answers as a spreadsheet, segmented
recipes.explanation: Cross-tabulates one scale question by a participant characteristic; the column totals reconcile against the server's own tally endpoint, so the numbers are checkable.

recipes.title: Decide whether to stop fielding
recipes.explanation: Shows where new interviews stopped contributing new language, which is the evidence for calling a study done rather than running it to an arbitrary quota.

recipes.title: Version a study definition
recipes.explanation: Captures details, welcome, screening, characteristics, questions or flow and recruitment as one file you can commit, diff and replay into a second study.

recipes.title: Check the rehearsal predicted reality
recipes.explanation: Compares simulated persona interviews against real ones on step reach, branch mix and variable capture, so a pilot becomes evidence rather than a vibe.

trigger_phrases: how did my interview flow route
export study answers as a table
compare my simulation to real interviews
